headline: Denied garages at 1549 Tuttle Avenue and 45 Country Club Lane, approved a garage at 38 Pieper Drive and a sign at 1 Dudley Avenue.
summary: Four requests sought larger garages, and three were denied. The board also approved a nail salon in an attic at 580 Gianotti Court, limited to 500 sq. ft. with one client at a time. It continued a side egress variance for 722 Center St. until November.
decisions: Denied special exception for a 1,662 sq. ft. total garage area at 1549 Tuttle Avenue, with a 3-2 vote in favor.
Denied variance for 13% building coverage at 1549 Tuttle Avenue, with a 2-3 vote.
Approved front yard setback variance of 44.2 feet for a front overhang at 17 Fawn Drive, unanimously.
Denied special exception for a 1,376 sq. ft. total garage area at 45 Country Club Lane, with a 3-2 vote in favor.
Approved special exception for a 1,464 sq. ft. total garage area at 38 Pieper Drive, unanimously.
Approved special exception for a 1,182 sq. ft. total sign area at 1 Dudley Avenue, unanimously.
Approved special exception for a nail salon in the home at 580 Gianotti Court, with conditions, unanimously.
Continued side yard setback variance request for 722 Center St. to the November meeting, unanimously.
Approved the July 20, 2026 meeting minutes as submitted, unanimously.

plain_text:
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 1 
 
Wallingford Zoning Board of Appeals 
October 19, 2026 
7:00 p.m. 
Robert F. Parisi Council Chambers 
Town Hall – 45 South Main Street 
 
Minutes 
Present:  Thomas Wolfer, Chairman; Bruce Conroy, Vice Chair; Robert Gross, Secretary;  Board 
Members: Raymond Rys; Chris Larocque; Robert Prentice; Rachel Shamaly, Land Use Specialist/Zoning 
Enforcement Officer; and Kevin Pagini, Town Planner.   
 
Chairman Wolfer called the meeting to order at approximately 7:00 p.m. The Pledge of Allegiance was 
recited.  
 
Voting members tonight are Conroy, Gross, Rys, Prentice, and Chairman Wolfer. 
 
Chairman Wolfer noted that tonight’s decisions will be published in the Record-Journal on Friday, 
October 23, 2026. The effective date of your variance will be Friday, October 23, 2026, the date a 
certified copy is recorded on the land records. The statutory 15-day appeal period will expire on Sunday, 
November 8, 2026. If you commence operations and/or construction during the appeal period, you do 
so at your own risk. 
 
PUBLIC HEARINGS 
1. #26-011/Special Exception Request/Gentile/Garage Area of 1,662 sq. ft. (max. 936 sq. ft. 
allowed) to construct a 1,200 sq. ft. detached garage at 1549 Tuttle Avenue in an RU-40 
District.  and 
2. #26-012/Variance Request/Gentile/Building Coverage of 13% (max. 10% allowed) to construct 
a 1,200 sq. ft. detached garage at 1549 Tuttle Avenue – RU-40 District. 
 
Mr. Gross read the staff notes into the record.  The applicant is requesting a Special Exception for a 
garage area and a Variance to increase building coverage on the property by 3% over what is allowed by 
right in the RU-40 zoning district. The property has ample space for the additional garage area; the 
proposed detached garage is height- and location-compliant.  The buildings and lot were created prior 
to the adoption of the Zoning Regulations in October of 1958 and therefore are undersized for the 
current zoning designation. Correspondence included a letter from OCC group received July 23, 2026, 
with the drawing and letter from Faris and Ashley Aruri, neighbors, received July 27, 2026. 
 
Mike Gentile, 1549 Tuttle Avenue, and Dominic DiMartino, 920 South Colony Road, explained the 
application. 
 
Mr. DiMartino explained that Mr. Gentile is a car collector and wants to bring all his cars to his property. 
The plans are for 1200 sq. ft. garage (30 ft. x 40 ft.) with a single door.  His neighbor to the left would be 
most affected and supports this.
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 2 
 
Chairman Wolfer asked what is stored in the other two garages.  Mr. Gentile replied that he has a total 
of 7 cars, but only two on the property now.  He also has a couple of antique motorcycles and has very 
little storage space in the house. He will not do repairs to the cars.   
 
Mr. Rys asked if there would be plumbing or drainage at the garage and if he would be doing any 
bodywork or mechanical work there. Mr. Gentile replied no. 
 
Mr. Gross asked if he would do oil or coolant changes.  Mr. Gentile replied no. Mr. Gross asked about 
paving up to the new garage. Mr. Gentile replied that the garage is at the end of the stone driveway. He 
may pave it in the future.  Mr. DiMartino explained that the garage will be 24 ft. ahead of the garage 
that exists.  It will be about 170 ft. away from the road.  Mr. Gentile added that the front of the new 
garage will be in line with the back of the house.  Mr. DiMartino stated that it is larger by 300 sq. ft.  Tall 
pine trees will block the view for all neighbors except one.  Mr. Gross noted that this is a large structure 
in a residential neighborhood. The two garages together will be larger than the house.  Mr. DiMartino 
disagreed.  Mr. Gross noted that the maximum coverage is 10% and this will make it 13%, as well as 
adding an impervious driveway.  Mr. DiMartino said the current gravel driveway will remain.  
 
Mr. Conroy asked about the hardship for the variance.  Mr. DiMartino replied that the zoning changed 3 
or 4 years ago. Mr. Pagini stated that there has been no change.  The application was required due to 
the size.  He noted that the lot is undersized for the district.  
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
None 
 
Hearing no public comment, Chairman Wolfer closed the public hearing and asked for discussion or 
possible action.  
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to approve application #26-011/Gentile/Special Exception/1549 Tuttle 
Avenue for a Special Exception Request for Total Garage Area of 1,662 sq. ft., where 462 Sq. 
Ft. exists and 936 sq. ft. maximum is permitted to construct a 1,200 sq. ft. detached garage at 
1549 Tuttle Avenue as shown on the Property Survey, showing the proposed detached garage 
on the property of Michael J. Gentile, 1549 Tuttle Avenue, dated August 20, 2024, and 
submitted plans received July 23, 2026.  
 
Mr. Rys: Second 
 
Vote:  Conroy – no to approve; Gross – no to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – yes to approve. 
The application is denied. 
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to approve application #26-012/Gentile/Variance Request/1549 Tuttle 
Avenue for a Variance Request for Building Coverage of 13% where 8% exists and a maximum 
of 10% is permitted to construct a 1,200 sq. ft. detached garage at 1549 Tuttle Avenue as 
shown on Property Survey, showing proposed detached garage on property of Michael J. 
Gentile, 1549 Tuttle Avenue, dated August 20, 2024 and submitted plans received July 23, 
2026. 
 
Mr. Rys: Second
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 3 
 
 
Vote:  Conroy – no to approve; Gross – no to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – no to approve. 
The application is denied. 
 
 
3. #26-013/Variance Request/Westbrook/Front Yard setback variance of 44.2 feet where 50 feet 
is required to construct a front door overhang at 17 Fawn Drive – RU-40 District. 
Mr. Gross read the staff notes into the record.  The applicant is requesting a variance to extend an 
addition for a front overhang approximately 6 feet into the required front yard setback in the RU-40 
zoning district. The overhang, as observed by a site visit, confirmed by the building department, as well 
as by the Assessor’s records, is already built. The Board should verify this with the applicant, and this 
approval would bring the applicant into compliance. The Board should make the applicant aware that 
they should receive the variance first before building any addition the next time around. 
 
Heather and Mike Westbrook, 17 Fawn Drive, presented. 
 
Chairman Wolfer confirmed that they received the stop work order from the Building Inspector. 
 
Ms. Westbrook explained that since receiving the order, they stopped work and followed the required 
steps to get here today. Mr. Westbrook stated that they had no intention to bypass the permit.  The 
house was re-sided and the roof redone.  It was an oversight. They thought the overhang was included 
in the permit for the siding. 
 
Mr. Gross confirmed that they had a permit for the siding and roof and that the same contractor did the 
overhang.   
 
Mr. Conroy clarified that the contractor didn’t include the overhang in the permit. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
None 
 
Hearing no public comment, Chairman Wolfer closed the public hearing and asked for discussion or 
possible action.  
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to approve application #26-013/Variance Request/Westbrook/17 Fawn 
Drive for a Variance Request for a front yard of 44.2 ft., where 50.3 ft. exists, and 50 ft. is 
required to construct a front overhang addition at 17 Fawn Drive as shown on Zoning Location 
Survey, property of Michael and Heather Westbrook, 17 Fawn Drive, dated May 1, 2026, and 
submitted plans received August 4, 2026. 
 
Mr. Rys: Second 
 
Vote:  Conroy – yes to approve; Gross – yes to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – yes to approve. 
The application is approved.
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 4 
 
4. #26-014/Special Exception Request/DeBaise/Garage Area of 1,376 sq. ft. (max. 936 sq. ft. 
allowed) to construct an 804 sq. ft. detached garage expansion at 45 Country Club Lane – R-18 
District.  
Mr. Gross read the staff notes into the record.  The applicant is requesting a Special Exception for a 
garage area to construct an expansion on a pre-existing 672 sq. ft. detached garage by 704 sq. ft. for a 
total area of 1,376 sq. ft. of garage area.  The property has ample space for the additional garage area; 
the proposed detached garage is height- and location-compliant. The second page of the application 
was corrected as the numbers didn’t match the square footage on the survey. 
 
Tim DeBaise, 25 Country Club Lane, explained that he has a 3-car garage that is full. He collects cars and 
needs storage. He is adding an additional 700 sq. ft. to the existing garage.  He will go back 13.3 ft. and 
8.6 ft. to the right. 
 
Chairman Wolfer asked if he would be doing any car repairs there.  Mr. DeBaise replied no. 
 
Mr. Gross asked for an explanation of the location.  Mr. DeBaise replied that he is adding on to the 
existing garage. It is now 22 ft. deep and 30 ft. wide.  It will be within the setback, so 20 ft. from the 
neighbor.  Mr. Gross noted that it will be 1,300 sq. ft. in total, which is a big garage for the 
neighborhood. He added that Mr. DeBaise is entitled to do a small addition.  Mr. Pagini stated that this 
is a bit more than what he is entitled to do.  He gets 936 sq. ft. by right and is only asking for 400 sq. ft. 
extra.  Mr. Gross noted that there is a trailer there.  Mr. DeBaise replied that it is not there all the time. 
He added that he has three collector cars plus needs room for storage.  He added that there is a house 
not too far away with a couple of big garages.  
 
Mr. Prentice asked if the neighbors had any issues with this. This will be seen from the road.  Mr. 
DeBaise replied no. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
None 
 
Hearing no public comment, Chairman Wolfer closed the public hearing and asked for discussion or 
possible action.  
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to approve application #26-014 – Special Exception Request/DeBaise/45 
Country Club Lane for a Special Exception request for Total Garage Area of 1,376 sq. ft. where 
672 sq. ft. exists and 936 sq. ft maximum is permitted to expand an existing 672 sq. ft. 
detached garage by another 704 sq. ft. at 45 Country Club Lane as shown on Property Survey, 
showing proposed detached garage expansion on property of Tim DeBaise, 45 Country Club 
Lane, dated August 2, 2026 and submitted plans received August 10, 2026. 
 
Mr. Rys: Second 
 
Vote:  Conroy – no to approve; Gross – no to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – yes to approve. 
The application is denied.
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 5 
 
5. #26-015/Special Exception Request/Kroher/Garage Area of 1,464 sq. ft. (max. 936 sq. ft. 
allowed) to construct an 884 sq. ft. detached garage at 38 Pieper Drive – R-18 District. 
Mr. Gross read the staff notes into the record.  The applicant is requesting a Special Exception for garage 
area to construct an 884± sq. ft. detached garage for a total area of 1,464± sq. ft. of garage area (an 
attached 528 ± sq. ft. garage currently exists). The property has ample space for the additional garage 
area; the proposed detached garage is height and location compliant. This application was heard at a 
previous meeting and was denied due to non-compliance with height requirements.  A closer look at this 
returning application revealed that the applicant had submitted the previous application with the wrong 
parcel survey and incorrect abutters.  The corrected application with the applicant’s correct lot of record 
gives them approximately another 3,000± sq. ft. compared to the previous application that was 
submitted. The lot that was submitted with the previous application was Lot 42 from the original Pieper 
Drive subdivision map in 1973, and the applicant’s actual lot is Lot 10. 
 
Mr. Pagini noted that the corrections have been made. This was an oversight by the Building 
Department. His property is actually Lot 10. He added that the height is now compliant. 
 
Tom Kroher, 38 Pieper Drive, stated that he is building a three-car garage because the existing garage is 
too small and he needs bigger doors for his vehicles. He also needs space for a wheelchair accessible van 
as well as two antique boats.   
 
Mr. Gross asked about the location and if the driveway is extended already. 
 
Mr. Pagini clarified that a Variance requires hardship.  A Special Exception is considered if it meets 
certain conditions such as fitting the neighborhood. 
 
Mr. Conroy noted that the lot size hasn’t changed much with the corrected lot number. He would like to 
see a smaller garage. 
 
Mr. Kroher noted that his neighbor was recently approved for a 30x40 garage. He showed photos of 
garages in the neighborhood. 
 
Ms. Shamaly noted that the existing attached garage is 528 sq. ft. and that a smaller proposal would be 
acceptable.  
 
Mr. Pagini noted that the Board can keep this application open to think about whether it is acceptable in 
the neighborhood.  Any accessibility question would be more of an accommodation. The Board can 
suggest changes as well. 
 
Chairman Wolfer stated that the Board can vote on what was presented or keep it open. He stated that 
he would like to see something smaller. Consensus was to vote. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
None 
 
Hearing no public comment, Chairman Wolfer closed the public hearing and asked for discussion or 
possible action.
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 6 
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to approve application #26-015 – Special Exception Request /Kroher/38 
Pieper Drive for a Special Exception request for Total Garage Area of 1,464 sq. ft. where 528 
sq. ft. exists and 936 sq. ft. maximum is permitted to construct an 884 sq. ft. detached garage 
at 38 Pieper Drive as shown on Property Survey map, showing proposed detached garage on 
property of Thomas Kroher, 38 Pieper Drive, and submitted plans received August 10, 2026. 
 
Mr. Conroy: Second 
 
Vote:  Conroy – yes to approve; Gross – yes to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – yes to approve. 
The application is approved. 
 
 
6. #26-016/Special Exception Request/Ulbrich Steel Inc./Sign Area of 1,182 sq. ft. (max. 682 sq. 
ft. allowed) at 1 Dudley Ave – I-20 District. 
Mr. Gross read the staff notes into the record.  The applicant is requesting a Special Exception for 
maximum sign area to install a 700± sq. ft. building sign for a total area of 1/182± sq. ft. of total sign 
area, where 682 sq. ft. is allowed.  The company has multiple buildings, and the additional signage 
would be placed on the side of the building and should not present a visual or aesthetic impediment to 
the surrounding area.  
 
Laurie Keily for 1 Dudley Avenue and John Ulbrich, 1 Dudley Avenue, presented.   
 
Mr. Ulbrich explained that they have been updating their cultural signage at their facilities around their 
purpose statement.  This will be a banner of their 100-year history.  It will be put in their highest traffic 
area between buildings to be seen by their workforce.   
 
Mr. Gross asked if it will be illuminated.  Ms. Keily replied no. They are just asking for additional square 
footage. The sign will not be facing the road. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
None 
 
Hearing no public comment, Chairman Wolfer closed the public hearing and asked for discussion or 
possible action.  
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to approve application #26-016 – Special Exception Request/Ulbrich Steel 
Inc./1 Dudley Ave for a Special Exception Request for Total Sign Area of 1,182 sq. ft. where 
482 sq. ft. exists to place a 700 sq. ft. building mounted sign at 1 Dudley Avenue as shown on 
documentation dated August 13, 2026, showing proposed signage on the property of Ulbrich 
Stainless Steel and Specialty Metals, 1 Dudley Avenue and submitted plans received August 
14, 2026. 
 
Mr. Conroy: Second 
 
Vote:  Conroy – yes to approve; Gross – yes to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – yes to approve. 
The application is approved.
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 7 
 
7. #26-017/Special Exception Request/Godinez/Customary Home Occupation – Nail Salon at 580 
Gianotti Ct. – R-6 District 
Mr. Gross read the staff notes into the record.  The applicant is requesting a Special Exception for a 
Customary Home Occupation – Nail Salon at 580 Gianotti Ct. in an R-6 District. The applicant has 
identified a location within the dwelling on the upper floor, which has approximately 660 sq. ft. total 
available, including a bathroom.  The Board should condition any approval on the use of no more than 
500 sq. ft. of the attic space for the home occupation use, which the Applicant has been made aware of 
before the meeting. The homeowner’s daughter, who is also a resident in the home, will be the sole 
employee, serving one customer at a time. Off-street parking is provided. No signage or retail services 
are proposed or permitted. 
 
Debra Godinez, 580 Gianotti Court, presented that they want to set her daughter up with a nail salon in 
the attic. This is to start her first business. 
 
Chairman Wolfer asked if they will overlap appointments.  Ms. Godinez replied no.  Chairman Wolfer 
clarified that there is enough parking. Ms. Godinez replied yes. Chairman Wolfer asked if they will be 
able to use only 500 sq. ft. of the available 600 sq. ft.  Ms. Godinez replied yes. 
 
Mr. Gross noted that it is all one open room. Ms. Godinez replied that there is nothing there now.  Mr. 
Gross asked Mr. Pagini if the town will go back and verify that they are only using 500 sq. ft.  Mr. Pagini 
replied that prior to a building permit, the Building Department will review the layout. Mr. Gross asked if 
they will abide by the 500 sq. ft. limit. Ms. Godinez said yes.   
 
Mr. Conroy confirmed that there will only be one client at a time.  Ms. Godinez agreed. 
 
Mr. Larocque asked if there are any plans to build a structure to limit it to 500 sq. ft.  Ms. Godinez 
replied that they will if they have to.   
 
Ms. Shamaly noted that this can be a condition of approval.   
 
Mr. Gross suggested a condition that there be only one client at a time. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
None 
 
Hearing no public comment, Chairman Wolfer closed the public hearing and asked for discussion or 
possible action.  
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to approve application #26-017 – Special Exception Request/Godinez/580 
Gianotti Ct. for a Special Exception Request for Customary Home Occupation – Nail Salon as 
shown on submitted plans at 580 Gianotti Court received September 9, 2026 and as shown on 
documentation received October 14, 2026, subject to the following conditions: 
1. Home occupation not to occupy more than the maximum 500 sq. ft. of available attic 
space. 
2. Only one customer permitted at a time. 
 
Mr. Conroy: Second
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 8 
 
Vote:  Conroy – yes to approve; Gross – yes to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – yes to approve. 
The application is approved. 
 
 
8. #26-018/Variance Request/McNulty/Side Yard setback variance of 3.91 feet where 12 feet is 
required to construct a side egress at 722 Center St., R-11 District. 
Mr. Gross read the staff notes into the record.  The applicant is requesting a Variance to build a covered 
side egress required by the Fire Department, approximately 8 feet 1 inches into the required side yard 
setback in the R-11 District. The house, built in 1898, predates the inception of zoning, and there is an 
existing non-conforming structure in the side yard setback (11.8’ where 12’ is required). This building 
was previously approved for conversion into a three-family home, and the Fire Marshal is requiring an 
independent egress to the third floor, with a 10’ separation buffer from the main house. The Applicant 
reviewed alternatives with the local Fire Marshal and Wallingford’s Chief Building Officer and 
determined that the proposed egress location is the only compliant location to meet fire code 
restrictions. 
 
Francis McNulty, 8 Salted Lane, Durham, presented.  He stated that he was approved two years ago for 
converting a two-family house into a three-family house.  He added a second stairway in the front to 
allow a second egress for the third floor. The Fire Marshal requires an independent egress for the third 
floor.  It was determined that the best option is to come off the second-floor landing. It has to be 10 feet 
off the side of the house and run to the back of the house.  He noted that he has more things to do for 
fire prevention as well.  The stairway will be just shy of 4 ft. from the property line, so the required stairs 
cut into the setback.  
 
Chairman Wolfer clarified that he worked with the Fire Marshal and the Building Department.  Mr. 
McNulty confirmed and noted that this was their recommendation. 
 
Mr. Larocque asked for the architectural drawings, which Mr. McNulty provided.   
 
Mr. Gross asked if there is already an apartment on the third floor. Mr. McNulty replied no. It is 
currently storage, and the second-floor apartment does not have permission to use the third floor.  Mr. 
Gross asked about the hardship. Mr. McNulty replied that the house was built in 1898. is not in the 
middle of the lot, and the property line is angled.  He has notes from all the abutting neighbors that they 
have no objection.  Mr. Gross noted that the hardship can’t be financial. Since he will be renting the 
apartment, he is doing it for profit. Ms. Shamaly noted that considerations are the inception of zoning 
and the geography of the lot. Financial is also part of the consideration. 
 
Mr. McNulty noted that the Town wants to increase housing density.  He is restricted in trying to make 
the house conform to the existing stairs, the lot shape, and the Fire Marshal’s request.  He stated that 
he couldn’t put the stairway out the back due to the Fire Marshal and the Building Department.  
 
Mr. Prentice asked if he could get the stairs closer. Mr. McNulty replied that there is a jut-out for the 
first floor bathroom.   The walls need to be fireproofed, and he will need to change the windows so they 
are fireproof.  Nothing will bring it closer than 10 ft.  
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
None
October 19, 2026 ZBA Minutes Page 9 
 
 
Hearing no public comment, Chairman Wolfer asked for discussion or possible action.  
 
Mr. Conroy noted that off the back would be more compliant. 
Mr. Gross agreed. 
 
Mr. Pagini stated that the application can be left open and we can ask the Fire Marshal to see if the back 
is an option.   
 
Mr. McNulty reported that he sent a letter to the Fire Marshal and the Building Department and gave 
them copies of everything.  He hasn’t heard back yet. 
 
Chairman Wolfer believes that the Fire Marshal told him to do it this way. 
 
Mr. Gross: Motion to continue application #26-018 – Variance Request/McNulty/722 Center 
Street to the November meeting to get clarification from the Fire Marshal on egress. 
 
Mr. Conroy: Second 
 
Vote:  Conroy – yes to approve; Gross – yes to approve; Rys – yes to approve; Prentice - yes to 
approve; and Chairman Wolfer – yes to approve. 
The application is continued. 
 
Ms. Shamaly reported that staff can reach out to the Fire Marshal.  
 
CONSIDERATION OF MINUTES 
 
1. July 20, 2026, Regular Meeting 
 
Mr. Rys: Motion to accept the July 20, 2026, Zoning Board of Appeals Minutes as submitted. 
 
Mr. Conroy: Second 
Vote:  Unanimous 
 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
Mr. Conroy: Motion to adjourn the October 19, 2026, regular meeting of the Zoning Board of 
Appeals at 8:20 p.m. 
 
Mr. Rys:  Second 
Vote:  Unanimous 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Cheryl-Ann Tubby 
Recording Secretary
